sections.h2: Why is Pickerington split between two counties?
sections.html:
Pickerington straddles Fairfield and Franklin counties, so your tax bill, auditor and treasurer depend on which side of the line the parcel falls. Wikipedia ranks it as the second-largest city in Fairfield County after Lancaster, yet a Pickerington address can still be billed by Franklin County.

The city was founded in 1815 as Jacksonville, renamed in 1827 for Abraham Pickering, certified as a city in 1991, and named the Violet Capital of Ohio by the legislature in 1996, according to Wikipedia. It sits about 840 feet above sea level just east of Columbus. The July 2025 federal estimate is 26,333 people, 14.1% above the 2020 estimates base of 23,070. Look up your parcel number before listing so you know which county offices to call.

sections.h2: How would you describe Pickerington's housing stock and buyers?
sections.html:
It is a family suburb with high owner occupancy and a high price point. Owners occupy 76.8% of homes in the 2020 to 2024 QuickFacts table, with a $339,600 midpoint value and $1,605 midpoint rent. There are 8,420 households of 2.89 people on average, and children under 18 are 27.5% of the population.

  • Median household income is $111,833 and per capita income is $46,372.
  • Workers spend 26.9 minutes getting to their jobs, typical of a commuter suburb.
  • OhioHealth Pickerington Methodist Hospital became a full-service hospital in December 2023, a plus for buyers who want medical care close by.

Buyers who use a mortgage face an appraisal and a lender's review, so a house that needs repairs can stall in a retail sale, which is where as-is offers come in.

sections.h2: How do Pickerington schools affect where buyers look?
sections.html:
Buyers sort by the Pickerington Local School District, which Wikipedia describes as 15 buildings: two high schools, an alternative high school, two junior highs, three middle schools, seven elementary schools and an early childhood center. The two main high schools are Pickerington High School Central and Pickerington High School North.

Elementary names in the district include Fairfield, Heritage, Pickerington, Violet, Tussing, Sycamore Creek and Toll Gate. When you write a listing, name the school buildings that serve the street, because families often search by building. Ask the district office to confirm attendance zones before you advertise them, since boundaries can change.

sections.h2: How has Pickerington grown, and what does the housing count show?
sections.html:
The city grew from 18,291 people in 2010 to 23,094 in 2020, and Wikipedia credits annexation, development and in-migration tied to Columbus. In 2020 it had 7,914 households and 8,373 housing units, 5.5% of them vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3% and the rental vacancy rate 13.3%, so empty owner-occupied houses are scarce while rentals sit open more often.

The median age was 35.5 in 2020 and 44.8% of households had children under 18. Newer subdivisions, the Olde Pickerington Village core and the Motorcycle Hall of Fame off Interstate 70 give the city several different faces, so describe the part of town your house sits in rather than the whole city.

sections.h2: What permits and codes apply to a Pickerington house?
sections.html:
The city Building Department reviews plans, issues permits and inspects structures, and it is certified by the Ohio Board of Building Standards to enforce the 2019 Residential Code of Ohio and the 2024 Ohio Building Code. Contractor registration and building permits are filed on the city's OpenGov portal.

If past work on the house, such as a deck or finished basement, was done without a permit, sort it out before a buyer's inspector asks. Code Enforcement answers questions at 614-833-2204.

sections.h2: How does Pickerington handle code complaints and vacant houses?
sections.html:
Code enforcement runs on complaints from residents, and the city lists examples such as grass above 6 inches on a developed lot, piled debris and structures that are not maintained. Property maintenance and junk vehicle cases can take up to a month of legal steps before the owner gets a summons to Mayor's Court.

Vacant and abandoned homes must be registered. The city lists an annual $150 fee, due January 1 and received no later than January 31, with no proration. The registration names the mortgagee and, for an out-of-area owner, the local property manager. A buyer of a bank-owned house is told to check lien information with the zoning officer. Owners are also responsible for clearing sidewalks and storm drains under Section 660.05 of the Pickerington Codified Ordinances.

sections.h2: How do Fairfield and Franklin County taxes work for a Pickerington seller?
sections.html:
Fairfield County states that taxable value is 35% of market value, and any levy above the ten-mill limit needed a vote. Franklin County parcels follow the same state system but are administered from Columbus. Call the Fairfield County Auditor at 740-652-7020 or the Franklin County Treasurer at 614-525-3438 for your parcel's dates before you pick a closing day.

Two Franklin County facts are on its Treasurer page: the second-half 2025 payment was due July 20, 2026, and appeals of 2026 property value can be filed with the Auditor from November 20, 2026 through March 31, 2027. For Fairfield owners, the Auditor's Homestead program exempts the first $29,000 of value for qualifying owners and wants a wet-signed application filed within the year. The credit does not follow a homeowner to a new house, so a seller moving within the area must apply again at the new address.

sections.h2: What should a Pickerington owner do first when a quick sale is the goal?
sections.html:
Start with the paperwork that only you can fix, then decide how to sell. A few checks save days later.

  • Find the parcel number and confirm whether Fairfield or Franklin County bills it.
  • Ask the Building Department about any permit that was never closed for a deck, basement or addition.
  • Check whether a vacant house still needs its annual $150 registration and whether a lien exists.
  • Find out if you hold a Homestead credit, since Fairfield County says it does not transfer to a new home.
  • Gather the school names that serve the street, the age of the roof and furnace, and any HOA rules.

With those answers in hand, a listing agent, a direct buyer or the county offices can each respond faster, and you can compare offers on the same facts.

sections.h2: Who should consider a cash sale in Pickerington?
sections.html:
Cash suits a seller who values a firm closing date over squeezing out extra price. At these values a lender will require an appraisal, and a buyer's inspection can reopen the price when the roof is old or a deck lacks a permit.

Direct buyers usually take the property in current condition, a help with an inherited house, a rental after a tenant leaves or a vacant house that needs registering. Request written offers from more than one buyer and ask who pays closing costs.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax on a Pickerington house?
faqs.a: It is Fairfield or Franklin County depending on the parcel, since the city spans both. Look up your parcel number and ask that county's treasurer for the due dates.

faqs.q: Does Pickerington require me to register a vacant house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires registration of abandoned or vacant homes with an annual fee of $150, due January 1 and received by January 31 each year.

faqs.q: How big is the Fairfield County Homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Qualifying owners can exempt the first $29,000 of appraised value, according to the Fairfield County Auditor. The form needs a wet signature and must be filed within the year the credit is sought.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pickerington house with an unpermitted deck?
faqs.a: You can, but a buyer's inspector may find it. The Building Department explains the permit steps, and a direct buyer may take the house as is.
The Census Bureau estimated 26,333 residents on July 1, 2025, up from 23,070 in April 2020. Households average 2.89 people.
